commit.message:
zpay32: fail TestBOLT11Vectors if an expected-error key matches no vector

In this commit, we make TestBOLT11Vectors assert that every key in
expectedVectorErrors and paymentLayerVectors names one of the loaded
vectors. Before, a key that matched nothing, due to a typo or a reworded
description after a resync from the spec repository, quietly dropped the
vector back to a bare require.Error check.

zpay32: document first-wins for repeated n and h fields

In this commit, we update the comments on repeated `n` and `h` fields.
A field with the wrong length is now an error rather than unsupported,
so "already seen a supported one" no longer describes why we skip it.
Keeping the first one is deliberate: BOLT 11 only requires exactly one
`p` and one `s` field.

zpay32: resync BOLT 11 vectors with bolts#1368

In this commit, we pick up the corrected high-S vector from
lightning/bolts#1368, which drops the duplicate `s` field it used to
carry. The vector now reaches the signature check, so we expect
`ErrHighSSignature` for it rather than `ErrDuplicatePaymentAddr`.

zpay32: assert why each fixed BOLT 11 vector is rejected

In this commit, we make the tests show that each of the new decoder
rules is what rejects its invalid invoice, rather than any error.

The vector test only checked that an invalid vector failed, so a vector
rejected for the wrong reason still passed. That hid a real gap: the
spec's high-S vector also repeats its `s` field, so it's rejected as a
duplicate payment address before the signature is ever checked, and no
test exercised `ErrHighSSignature` at all.

We now map each vector this PR fixes to the sentinel error it must
produce, and add `TestDecodeHighSWithDestination`, which decodes the
same invoice (with a single `s` field) once with a high-S and once with
a low-S signature. A duplicate `s` case joins `TestParseTaggedFields`.
Dropping or breaking any of the three new checks now fails a test aimed
at it.

commit.message:
htlcswitch: avoid per-row queries when pruning network result store

The network result store is pruned at startup, keeping only results for
payments that are still in flight. Previously, cleanStore iterated over
the bucket and deleted each stale key individually.

On SQL backends, each iteration step and deletion requires separate
database queries. A store with N entries therefore incurred O(N)
sequential client/server round trips and could make startup take hours
when using remote PostgreSQL.

Read retained results with one streaming query, drop and recreate the
bucket, then restore the retained entries. PostgreSQL still processes
O(N) rows internally, but the operation no longer performs a round trip
for every stored result.

Exercise cleanup across the supported kvdb backends, including partial,
empty, and unchanged result sets. Add PostgreSQL benchmarks covering
1,000 and 10,000 entries with fully stale and partially retained stores.

Fixes #11353.

Co-authored-by: ziggie <ziggie1984@protonmail.com>

commit.message:
sqldb/v2: fix lint issues

Fix the issues reported by the linter for the sqldb/v2 submodule so it
passes make lint-module.

Test helpers now use t.Context() instead of context.Background(), the
redundant copies of loop variables are removed, counter loops use
range-over-int, long lines are wrapped, and the whitespace around
returns follows the nlreturn and whitespace linters. The unused
defaultMigrateOptions helper is removed.

The retry backoff multiplies the initial delay with a factor that is
typed as a duration but is a plain multiplier, so the multiplication is
annotated with a nolint directive for durationcheck.

commit.message:
sqldb: fix lint issues

Fix the issues reported by the linter for the sqldb submodule so it
passes make lint-module.

Tests now use t.Context() instead of context.Background(), counter
loops use range-over-int, long lines are wrapped, and the whitespace
around returns follows the nlreturn and whitespace linters. The
migration tests use errors.Is to compare against ErrNilVersion, and a
duplicated word in a comment is removed. The migration file prefix check
uses strings.HasPrefix to keep the line within the limit.

ApplyMigrations no longer assigns an initial value to currentVersion
that is always overwritten. The isSQLite test constant is only used by
tests built with the test_db_sqlite or test_db_postgres tags, so it is
annotated with a nolint directive for the default build.
